title: A Signal for the Echo
premise: Dominic Quintana smuggles memories—stolen lives, black-market grief—through the decaying orbital customs ring above Meridian Colony, a place the corporate fleets have written off as a rounding error. When the long-lost deep-space vessel Cassiopeia returns with its crew mysteriously aged backward, both rival fleets converge on Meridian, each ready to destroy the colony to claim the ship's secret. Dominic discovers the reversal was no accident but a desperate experiment by the colony's forgotten founders, and that the truth could either ignite a war or end one. To save the people who became her family, she fabricates and broadcasts a false memory of mutual destruction, holding the fleets at bay long enough for the colony's real signal—its plea for justice and belonging—to finally be heard. In the end, Meridian wins recognition not through the lie, but through Dominic's choice to confess it, trading her freedom for the colony's future.
about_author: K. M. Zhou is the pen name of a former maritime radio operator turned novelist who writes about people who live in the gaps between jurisdictions. Zhou's fiction has appeared in several genre magazines and draws on a childhood spent in port cities where every flag was negotiable.

chapters.title: Contraband of the Heart
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. She runs a memory-chip shipment past customs on the rotting Meridian ring, hiding contraband inside her own recorded grief for her dead brother. Establishes her trade, her cynicism, and the colony's quiet abandonment. Emotional beat: loneliness disguised as competence.

chapters.title: The Customs of Forgetting
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. A customs inspector, Ilsa Voss, nearly catches her and instead offers a bribe: look away from a fleet survey team arriving at Meridian. Dominic refuses and immediately regrets it. Emotional beat: the first crack in her careful neutrality.

chapters.title: Everyone Aboard Was Younger
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. The derelict Cassiopeia, missing forty years, docks unbidden—its crew alive, healthy, and decades younger than their records. The colony erupts; the fleets mobilize. Emotional beat: wonder curdling into dread.

chapters.title: What the Founders Buried
chapters.summary: Founders' archive POV, framed as a recovered memory Dominic plays. Reveals Meridian's founders ran a forbidden longevity experiment and erased themselves from fleet records to protect it. Emotional beat: inherited guilt.

chapters.title: Two Fleets, One Harbor
chapters.summary: Ilsa Voss's POV. The Concord and the Verity fleets arrive in uneasy joint blockade, each claiming salvage rights. Voss, ordered to seize Dominic's smuggling network, instead quietly warns her. Emotional beat: an enemy becoming something else.

chapters.title: The Girl Who Was Old Once
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. She meets Sefa, the Cassiopeia's navigator, now biologically twelve but carrying forty years of memories. Sefa begs Dominic to smuggle her memories out before the fleets take the crew. Emotional beat: tenderness toward a child who is not one.

chapters.title: Price of a Clean Record
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. The fleets offer Dominic full amnesty to hand over the crew's memory archives. She stalls, buying time while the colony's elders argue over surrender. Emotional beat: temptation of the easy exit.

chapters.title: Found Family, Forged Papers
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV, rotating through Dominic's smuggler crew as they forge identities for the reversed crew. The found-family theme crystallizes: people with no records making records for each other. Emotional beat: warmth under pressure.

chapters.title: The Lie That Could Hold
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. She conceives the plan: fabricate a shared memory proving both fleets' admirals already agreed to joint custody—so neither can attack without breaking the other's trust. Emotional beat: fear and resolve braided together.

chapters.title: Interrogation of a Smuggler
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. Voss formally interrogates Dominic and realizes the plan, choosing not to report it—a career-ending act of complicity. Emotional beat: justice chosen over law.

chapters.title: Signal Decay
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. The reversed crew begins losing memories at accelerating speed—the reversal is killing their pasts. Sefa's forty years are dissolving; she asks Dominic to remember her for her. Emotional beat: grief for a self still alive.

chapters.title: The Colony That Nobody Claimed
chapters.summary: Elder Tomas Reyes's POV. Meridian's council votes to surrender the crew rather than be destroyed; Reyes alone argues the colony's worth isn't negotiable. Emotional beat: dignity against despair.

chapters.title: Forging the Past
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. The crew crafts the false memory, and Dominic must record her own face and voice as the 'witness'—binding her fate to the lie. Emotional beat: crossing a point of no return.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. She injects the fabricated memory into both fleets' command relays during a joint ceremony. It holds—for now. Emotional beat: exhilaration shadowed by guilt.

chapters.title: Cracks in the Fabrication
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. A Concord analyst finds a timestamp anomaly. Voss must decide whether to bury the evidence or let the lie collapse. Emotional beat: loyalty tested against truth.

chapters.title: Sefa's Last Clear Day
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. Her memories of the deep-space voyage nearly gone, she records a final testimony revealing the founders meant the reversal as a gift, not a weapon. Emotional beat: grace in dissolution.

chapters.title: The Fleets Close In
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. The anomaly leaks; both fleets accuse the other of forgery and arm for bombardment. The lie that held them apart now drives them to war. Emotional beat: catastrophic reversal.

chapters.title: Everything I Stole
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Out of options, she broadcasts her entire smuggling archive—every stolen memory, including her brother's death and the fabrication itself—as proof of who she is and what she did. Emotional beat: self-destruction as testimony.

chapters.title: The Truth Is a Weapon Too
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. Voss presents Dominic's confession alongside Sefa's testimony to the joint fleet command, arguing the colony's crime was committed to give life, not take it. Emotional beat: the law bending toward justice.

chapters.title: Meridian Speaks
chapters.summary: Reyes's and Sefa's POV, interleaved. The colony transmits its own signal—forty years of ordinary lives, unedited—to both fleets. The bombardment orders stall. Emotional beat: the forgotten making themselves undeniable.

chapters.title: A Signal for the Echo
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. The fleets stand down; Meridian gains provisional recognition, and the reversed crew receives sanctuary. Dominic surrenders to Voss for sentencing, asking only that the colony keep her brother's memory in its archive. Emotional beat: sacrifice with open eyes.

chapters.title: Echoes, Answered
chapters.summary: Sefa's and Voss's POV, closing frame. A year later, Meridian thrives; Voss, now the colony's advocate, visits Dominic in custody with Sefa's new memories—childhood ones, real ones. Dominic finally belongs somewhere she'll never see free. Emotional beat: belonging earned, hope deferred but alive.
